subject: business-studies
title: SWOT Analysis
welcome_lead: Internal strengths and weaknesses; external opportunities and threats.
meta_desc: A-Level Analysis: SWOT framework and its quadrants.
final_note: SWOT is a starting point - it has to drive decisions to be worth the time.

concepts.def: Internal capabilities the firm can build.
External openings the firm can exploit.
Strengths and weaknesses - within firm control.
Opportunities and threats - outside firm control.

walkthroughs.body_html: SWOT divides factors into internal (S, W) and external (O, T). Strengths could be brand or technology; threats could be new entrants or recession.
Strong SWOT analyses pair quadrants - using a strength to seize an opportunity, or fixing a weakness before it meets a threat. This is the SO/WO/ST/WT matrix.
SWOT lists tend to be opinionated not evidence-based. Force every claim to be backed by data, customer research or a competitor benchmark.

mcqs.q: Are opportunities and threats internal to the business?
options: A talented workforce counts as an opportunity in SWOT.
No — in SWOT, strengths and weaknesses are internal, while opportunities and threats come from the external environment, like new markets or new regulations.
Threats in SWOT only refer to crime against the business.
Opportunities are listed only by the HR department.

mcqs.q: Does completing a SWOT or PESTLE analysis tell a business what to do?
options: Threats in SWOT only refer to crime against the business.
A finished SWOT diagram is itself a strategy.
SWOT results are legally binding for one year.
No — they organise information; managers must still weigh, prioritise and act on the findings, and the analysis dates quickly as conditions change.

mcqs.q: Is the same external factor always a threat?
options: No — one trend, such as new technology or a law change, can threaten one firm and create an opportunity for another, depending on its strengths.
SWOT results are legally binding for one year.
External factors are objectively either opportunities or threats for everyone.
Threats in SWOT only refer to crime against the business.
